record.paper_title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Causal imitation and transfer in MARL
record.original_question: In multi-agent knowledge sharing, when can causal imitation learning, causal transfer learning, and data fusion determine whether one agent can imitate or learn from a more knowledgeable teacher agent, which variables are important for imitation, and what performance should be expected?

evidence.quote: Another promising method of knowledge sharing is by applying transfer learning and imitation learning. In these settings, a more knowledgeable agent shares or teaches acquired knowledge to another agent (Pan and Yang, 2010).

An exciting CRL research direction is that of causal imitation learning where a causal model of the environment can be used to determine when imitation is feasible, and what performance we can expect.

Reasoning causally has shown to aid in determining what variables are important for the imitation procedure (Zhang et al., 2020). Tying these ideas together with (causal) transfer learning and data-fusion opens room for exciting research avenues.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-agent decision-making setting modeled as a Markov game with $n$ agents. Each agent $i$ has its own observation space $\mathcal{O}_i$, action space $\mathcal{A}_i$, and policy $\pi_i$. Suppose one designated agent (the "teacher") $T$ has access to a policy $\pi_T$ that achieves expected return $V^{\pi_T}$ in some environment described by a structural causal model (SCM) $\mathcal{M}_T = (U_T, V_T, F_T, P(U_T))$, where $V_T$ are endogenous variables (states, actions, rewards), $U_T$ are exogenous variables, and $F_T$ are structural assignments. A second agent (the "learner") $L$ operates in an environment described by an SCM $\mathcal{M}_L$ that may differ from $\mathcal{M}_T$ in observation availability, intervention set, or causal mechanisms. The learner observes only demonstration trajectories $\{(o_t^T, a_t^T)\}_{t\ge 0}$ from $\pi_T$ together with possibly heterogeneous datasets $\mathcal{D}_1,\dots,\mathcal{D}_k$ collected from related environments under different interventions.

Provide a formal framework, drawing on causal imitation learning, causal transfer learning, and causal data fusion, that answers all of the following:

(a) Imitability criterion. Give necessary and sufficient graphical/structural conditions on $(\mathcal{M}_T, \mathcal{M}_L)$ and on the learner's observable variables under which there exists a learner policy $\pi_L$ such that the imitation gap $V^{\pi_T} - V^{\pi_L}$ can be made zero (or bounded) using only the demonstrations and auxiliary datasets.

(b) Variable selection. Characterize the minimal subset $S \subseteq V_T$ of variables that the learner must observe and condition on so that imitating $\pi_T$ via $S$ is sound, identifying when latent confounders between $S$ and the teacher's action prevent valid imitation.

(c) Performance guarantees. Derive expected-return bounds on $V^{\pi_L}$ as a function of (i) the discrepancy between $\mathcal{M}_T$ and $\mathcal{M}_L$, (ii) the sample sizes of the demonstration and fusion datasets, and (iii) identifiability of the relevant causal effects across environments.

The problem is to formulate this framework, state and prove the corresponding identifiability and feasibility theorems, and produce matching upper and lower bounds on the achievable imitation performance in the multi-agent setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in causal multi-agent reinforcement learning. While single-agent causal imitation learning (e.g., work by Zhang, Kumor, and Bareinboim) provides graphical criteria for imitability and variable selection in the single-agent case, no comprehensive multi-agent framework unifying causal imitation, causal transfer, and causal data fusion with matching performance guarantees appears to have been established as of 2026. The problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Causal Imitation Learning with Unobserved Confounders
status_evidence.snippet: Provides graphical criteria for when an imitator can match an expert's performance in a single-agent SCM with unobserved confounders.
status_evidence.claim: Single-agent causal imitation feasibility has been characterized, but multi-agent extensions remain open.

status_evidence.title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists causal imitation learning, transfer learning, and data fusion in multi-agent settings as open research avenues.
status_evidence.claim: The combined multi-agent question is identified as an open direction.
